subject: Private connectivity: deployment mode + allowlist next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finbank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap and next steps — deployment mode & networking asks

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks again for the call this morning — useful run through of FinBank's latency and regulatory constraints. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary from our side:
- FinBank prefers Private deployment for production (Private VPC with PrivateLink preferred over peering) due to audit/compliance requirements.
- Primary workloads: real-time transaction enrichment (p95 latency target ~80ms) and nightly batch embeddings.
- NetOps will own allowlist and routing; app team will manage keys and secrets.

Redwood asks / open items:
1) Confirm preferred connectivity pattern: PrivateLink (endpoint in your VPC) vs VPC Peering. You mentioned PrivateLink during the call — can you confirm?
2) Allowlist: we need egress IPs for our customer-facing egress. Are you managing allowlist on your side or should we provide static egress IP ranges?
3) TLS termination and SNI / hostname expectations.
4) Proposed tech deep-dive: 60 minute session with FinBank NetOps + Redwood infra (we can share network diagram and minimal packet flow). Suggested slots: Mon/Tue next week — I can send a calendar invite if that works.

I've attached a lightweight network diagram that shows the two connectivity options (PrivateLink and peering) and a one-page spreadsheet of the specific questions NetOps asked on the call.

Next steps (proposed):
- Sanjay to confirm PrivateLink preference and NetOps contact.
- NetOps to confirm whether they want Redwood to own egress IPs or if FinBank will add Redwood ranges.
- Schedule tech deep-dive with NetOps (we propose calendar invite after confirmation).

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Meera Iyer <meera.iyer@finbank.com>, FinBank NetOps <netops@finbank.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap and next steps — deployment mode & networking asks

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few points: 

- We are leaning strongly toward PrivateLink. Our security team prefers it because it avoids cross-VPC routing and is simpler to audit.
- NetOps (copied) will take the lead on allowlisting. Meera (app infra) will coordinate certs.
- Regarding egress IPs: we typically require static ranges for vendor services. Would Redwood be able to provide a set of stable egress IPs or a small CIDR block we can allowlist? If not, we may need to stand up an internal NAT gateway to constrain egress.

NetOps — can you confirm you saw the attachments and propose availability for a 60-minute dive next Tue or Wed afternoon PST?

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Sr. PM, Platform Engineering | FinBank
+sanjay.patel@finbank.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finbank.com>, Meera Iyer <meera.iyer@finbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap and next steps — deployment mode & networking asks

Hi Sanjay / Meera — diving into a bit more detail from the infra side so your NetOps team has what they need to triage: 

Short answers:
- We can support PrivateLink or Peering. PrivateLink is the smoother path for smoke-tested production SLOs but requires endpoint config in your VPC and an allowlist of our egress.
- Redwood can provide a small set (4) of stable egress IPs from our edge egress pool (these are NATed and reserved per-customer in Private deployments). If you need an entire CIDR, we can discuss a managed NAT box as an option.

Network/ops checklist we will cover in the deep-dive:
- Egress IPs we propose to supply: 34.208.112.48, 34.208.112.49, 34.208.112.50, 34.208.112.51 (these are examples — we'll reserve on sign-off).
- Ports: 443 outbound to our service endpoints; inbound not required.
- Hostname: api.private.redwood.com (we will provide TLS certs; if you require mutual TLS, we support mTLS as an option).
- VPC endpoint policies: we can provide a sample policy to restrict access to model-serving API only.

Action: Jonas — if NetOps confirms PrivateLink + allowlist on their side, we'll prepare a short runbook and the sample endpoint policy to share ahead of the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
[attachment: runbook_template.md (text)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Tech deep-dive agenda + material to review before call

Hi all — looping in some concrete agenda items so the deep-dive is efficient. Please review the attached spreadsheet (finbank_nw_reqs.xlsx) before we meet. Proposed 60-minute agenda: 

1) 10m — Introductions & goals (FinBank security/NetOps)
2) 15m — Redwood PrivateLink architecture and packet flow (Vanessa)
3) 20m — Allowlist, IPs, and egress options (Aditya)
4) 10m — Certs, TLS, and optional mTLS (Meera + Vanessa)
5) 5m — Action items and owners (Jonas)

Proposed times (PST):
- Tue Jul 6: 2:00pm — 3:00pm
- Wed Jul 7: 11:00am — 12:00pm

If those don't work, suggest alternative windows and we'll adjust. Also: we will bring a short packet-capture example so NetOps can confirm there are no unexpected flows.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks team — we reviewed the attachments. Confirming:
- FinBank prefers PrivateLink.
- We will add Redwood egress IPs to our allowlist. Please provide the final (non-example) IPs and the FQDN(s) you will present traffic from.
- We are available Tue Jul 6 2:00pm PST for the deep-dive. 

I've attached a slightly annotated copy of your network diagram with our internal VPC IDs and the preferred endpoint subnet highlighted. 

See you on Tue.
